descriptionChirho: To join, attach, or connect objects together, especially used of joining curtains, boards, or other physical items (Piel active and related forms).
To be in a state of being joined, attached, or connected together, as a passive or resultative condition (Qal participle, Pual, and passive forms).
To ally oneself with another, form a political or interpersonal partnership or alliance (Hitpael reflexive and Qal/Piel with personal objects).
To bind or cast spells, practice sorcery or enchantment, referring to one who binds magical charms (Qal participle in contexts of forbidden divination).
To join or string words together in speech, to compose arguments or marshal rhetoric against someone (Hifil cohortative, Job 16:4).
